2027-07-03.title: Dukrono of St Thomas the Apostle
readings: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
Go from your country to the land I will show you
The path of the righteous is like the light of dawn
Oh, that I knew where I might find him
How beautiful are the feet of the messenger
Live as free people, as servants of God
In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel
2027-07-03.alt: Dukrono (commemoration) of St Thomas the Apostle, Father in Faith of the Church in India: Holy Qurbono for the people. St Thomas Day.
2027-07-03.verse: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
theo: On the evening of Easter Thomas was not with the others. When they told him, “We have seen the Lord,” he said: “Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my finger in the mark of the nails and my hand in his side, I will not believe.” A week later Jesus came again and said to him: “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe.” Thomas answered: “My Lord and my God!” It is the fullest confession of faith in the Gospels: the risen Jesus is Lord and God.

Jesus answered: “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That blessing is for us. The faith of India was not built on seeing but on the word of the apostle who saw, touched and believed. According to the ancient tradition of our Church, Thomas came to Kerala around AD 52, preached, founded communities, and gave his life as a martyr at Mylapore around AD 72. We are Thomas Christians, Mar Thoma Nasranikal.

At the Last Supper it was Thomas who asked: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” And Jesus gave the great answer: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” The questioner became the witness; the one who wanted proof travelled the furthest of all the apostles to give it.

Abraham left his country for a land God would show him; Thomas left Galilee for India. Isaiah sings: “How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news.” Paul writes: “In Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.” Thomas is our father in faith. Today we thank God for him and ask for his courage to confess Jesus as Lord and God in our own land.
conn: Abraham's journey.
Genesis 12: leaving home at God's word; Thomas travels to the ends of the earth for Christ.
Beautiful feet.
Isaiah 52:7: the messenger on the mountains; Thomas on the mountain at Mylapore.
Father in faith.
1 Corinthians 4:15: a father through the gospel; Thomas, father of the Church in India.
Seeking God.
Job 23:3: “Oh, that I knew where I might find him!”; Thomas asks the way and finds it in Christ.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono we do what Thomas did: we see with the eyes of faith the risen Lord who shows us his wounds, and we say, as the priest elevates the Mysteries, “My Lord and my God.”
outline: Point 2 · My Lord and my God
Point 4 · Blessed are those who have not seen
live: Make his confession yours
Say “My Lord and my God” at the elevation of the Holy Mysteries.
Visit a Thomas shrine
If possible, pray at a church linked with St Thomas, or pray for the whole Church in India.
Bring your doubts to Jesus
Bring an honest question to prayer instead of walking away from faith.
fathers: St Gregory the Great
The unbelief of Thomas has done more for our faith than the faith of the believing disciples; by touching he healed in us the wound of unbelief (Homilies on the Gospels 26).
St Ephrem the Syrian
Ephrem sings of the bones of the Apostle brought from India to Edessa by a merchant, and of Thomas who enlightened India (Nisibene Hymns 42).
magis: Catechism 644–645
The risen Jesus invites the disciples to touch him; Thomas confesses him Lord and God.
Catechism 448
The title “Lord” in the confession of Thomas expresses divine sovereignty.
Orientalium Ecclesiarum 1, 3
The Catholic Church holds in high esteem the institutions, rites and traditions of the Eastern Churches, which are of equal dignity.
saints: Sunday 4 July: VII Sunday after Pentecost. 6 July: St Maria Goretti. 11 July: St Benedict. 15 July (Thu): Commemoration of the Servant of God Archbishop Mar Ivanios.
2027-07-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, you showed your wounds to Thomas and led him from doubt to faith. Through his prayers keep us faithful to the faith he brought to India; make us witnesses in our land, and let our lives say with him: “My Lord and my God.” Amen.

2027-07-04.title: Seventh Sunday after Pentecost
readings: By your words you will be justified
The glory has departed from Israel
Their deeds do not permit them to return
Peace, peace, to the far and the near
The place was shaken; they spoke the word with boldness
He is our peace; the dividing wall broken down
A house divided against itself cannot stand
2027-07-04.verse: If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
theo: When Jesus casts out demons, some scribes say he does it by the ruler of demons. Jesus answers: “If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.” Satan divides; Christ unites. Wherever the Spirit is at work, he builds communion: in hearts, families, parishes and between Churches.

Jesus then gives a solemn warning: “Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven for their sins and whatever blasphemies they utter; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit can never have forgiveness.” The Church teaches that this is not a sin too great for God's mercy, but the refusal to accept that mercy: calling the Spirit's work evil and so closing the door through which forgiveness comes. In the evening Gospel Jesus adds: “by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

St Paul tells the Ephesians that Christ “is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.” Jews and Gentiles, once far apart, are now “citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.” Isaiah had promised: “Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.”

The first Christians, threatened by the authorities, did not divide or despair. They prayed together: “Lord, look at their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness.” “When they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.” United prayer brings the Spirit; the Spirit brings courage.
conn: Atonement.
Leviticus 16: the Day of Atonement cleansed the people once a year; Christ's blood reconciles us once for all (Ephesians 2:13).
Glory departed.
1 Samuel 4:21–22: “Ichabod”, the glory has gone, when Israel was unfaithful; the glory returns in Christ, and dwells in the Church as God's temple (Ephesians 2:21–22).
A house divided.
Mark 3:25 and Ephesians 2:14: division is the devil's work; Christ breaks down the dividing wall.
Bold prayer.
Acts 4:31: the house shaken by the Spirit, the opposite of the divided house.
altar: “In Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.” At the Holy Qurbono the sign of peace is exchanged before the anaphora: we cannot offer the one sacrifice while divided from our brother.
outline: Point 2 · The sin against the Spirit
Refusing mercy; the power of our words.
live: Heal one division
Take one step toward reconciliation in your family or parish this week.
Guard your words
Avoid one careless or harsh word each day; “by your words you will be justified.”
Pray for Christian unity
Pray for the unity of the Churches of the Thomas tradition in Kerala.
fathers: St Augustine
The sin against the Holy Spirit is impenitence: a heart that refuses to the end the forgiveness the Spirit offers in the Church (Sermon 71).
St John Chrysostom
Christ did not only make peace between us and God, but between us and one another, removing the wall of enmity (Homilies on Ephesians 5).
magis: Catechism 1864
There are no limits to God's mercy, but anyone who deliberately refuses to accept it by repenting rejects forgiveness and the salvation offered by the Holy Spirit.
Catechism 820–822
Christ bestows unity on his Church; the desire to recover the unity of all Christians is a gift of Christ and a call of the Spirit.
Unitatis Redintegratio 1
Division openly contradicts the will of Christ and is a scandal to the world.
saints: 6 July: St Maria Goretti. 11 July: St Benedict. Sunday 11 July: VIII Sunday after Pentecost. 15 July (Thu): Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios.
2027-07-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are our peace; you broke down the dividing wall of hostility. Heal the divisions in our hearts, families, parishes and Churches. Guard our tongues, keep us open to the mercy of your Spirit, and fill us with boldness to speak your word. Amen.

2027-07-11.title: Eighth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: Let anyone with ears to hear listen
Oh, that I knew where I might find him
Obey my voice, and I will be your God
My servants shall sing for gladness of heart
A chosen race, a royal priesthood
The word of God is living and active
Those who hear the word and accept it bear fruit
2027-07-11.alt: Season of Pentecost. (The 2025–26 lectionary lists Mark 4 for both Gospels; check the 2026–27 lectionary.)
2027-07-11.verse: Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
theo: “Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword… able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.” God's word is not a dead letter; it cuts, heals, judges and gives life. When the Gospel is proclaimed in the Qurbono, Christ himself speaks. The question is not whether the word is powerful, but whether we listen.

In Mark's Gospel Jesus begins his teaching by the sea with one word: “Listen!” Then the sower goes out to sow. The seed is the word; the soil is the human heart. “And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.” And he ends: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!” Listening is the first act of faith.

At the burning bush God speaks to Moses and reveals his name: “I AM WHO I AM… This is my name forever.” God is not an idea; he is the living One who speaks and sends: “I will be with you.” Jeremiah repeats God's one demand: “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people.” To obey (in Latin ob-audire) is to listen deeply.

The Letter to the Hebrews joins the Word with mercy: “We do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathise with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy.” St Peter tells us who we have become by listening and believing: “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people.”
conn: I AM.
Exodus 3:14: the divine name; Jesus speaks with the same authority: “Listen!”
Obey my voice.
Jeremiah 7:23: the covenant is listening; Mark 4:20: the good soil hears and accepts.
Seeking God.
Job 23:3: Job longs to find God; Hebrews 4:16: in Christ we may approach the throne with boldness.
A royal priesthood.
1 Peter 2:9: the people formed by the Word to declare God's wonders.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Word is first proclaimed, then made flesh on the altar. The same Christ who speaks in the Gospel gives himself in the Mysteries; the hearing of the Word prepares the heart to receive the Bread.
outline: “Listen!”: the first word of the parable.
The Word cuts, heals and judges.
The God who speaks and sends.
A high priest who understands our weakness.
“Let anyone with ears to hear listen!”
live: Ten minutes with the Word
Read the Sunday Gospel again each day this week, slowly, for ten minutes.
Listen to someone
Give one person your full attention this week, without interrupting.
Approach with boldness
Bring a weakness you are ashamed of to Christ in confession.
fathers: St Jerome
Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ (Commentary on Isaiah, Prologue).
St Ephrem the Syrian

Who can grasp all the richness of even one of your words, Lord? What we understand is much less than what we leave behind, like the thirsty who drink from a fountain (Commentary on the Diatessaron 1, 18).
magis: Catechism 131–133
The Church strongly exhorts all the faithful to learn the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ by frequent reading of the divine Scriptures.
Dei Verbum 21
In the sacred books the Father who is in heaven meets his children with great love and speaks with them.
Catechism 1546
The whole community of believers is, as such, priestly (1 Peter 2:9).
saints: 11 July: St Benedict. 15 July (Thu): Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios (1953): Holy Qurbono for the people. 16 July: Our Lady of Mount Carmel.
2027-07-11.prayer: Lord God, I AM WHO I AM, your word is living and active. Open our ears to listen, our hearts to accept, and our lives to bear fruit thirty, sixty and a hundredfold. Through Jesus, our merciful high priest, let us approach your throne of grace with boldness. Amen.

2027-07-15.title: Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios
readings: Well done, good and trustworthy slave
Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there
Keep watch over the flock; it is more blessed to give
Remember your leaders; imitate their faith
2027-07-15.alt: Commemoration of Archbishop Geevarghese Mar Ivanios (died 15 July 1953), founder and first Metropolitan Archbishop of the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church: Holy Qurbono for the people. His cause for canonisation is in progress; his tomb is at St Mary's Cathedral, Pattom, Thiruvananthapuram.
2027-07-15.verse: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
theo: The Letter to the Hebrews says: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” Today the Syro-Malankara Church remembers her father, Archbishop Mar Ivanios, who died on 15 July 1953. We remember him not to look back, but to imitate his faith.

Geevarghese, born in 1882 at Mavelikara, was a brilliant scholar and teacher. Drawn to prayer and to the monastic life, he founded the Bethany Ashram (Order of the Imitation of Christ) in 1919 and the Bethany Sisters in 1925. Longing for the unity of the Church, he searched for the communion of the Malankara Church with the See of Peter. On 20 September 1930, with Bishop Mar Theophilos and a few companions, he was received into full communion with the Catholic Church, keeping the venerable West Syriac liturgy. In 1932 he became the first Archbishop of Trivandrum.

Like Abraham and Moses, he left security behind. The reunion cost him churches, properties and friends; he began again in poverty, in small chapels and simple houses. Like the servant in the parable who traded with his talents, he did not bury what he had received: his learning, his liturgy, his love for the Malankara tradition became a gift to the universal Church. “Well done, good and trustworthy slave; you have been trustworthy in a few things, I will put you in charge of many things.”

Paul's farewell to the elders of Ephesus could be his: “Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son… remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’” Today we thank God for him, pray for the unity of all Christians, and ask God, if it is his will, to glorify his servant.
conn: Moses' death.
Deuteronomy 34: Moses sees the promised land and dies; Mar Ivanios led his people into communion and died having seen the Church grow.
I will be with you.
Exodus 3:12: God sends Moses with this promise; the same promise sustained the reunion movement.
Honour the priests.
Sirach 7:29–30: love and honour the Lord's ministers.
The faithful servant.
Matthew 24:45: the servant set over the household to give them food at the proper time.
altar: Mar Ivanios loved the West Syriac Holy Qurbono and brought it whole into Catholic communion. Every time we celebrate it in Malayalam, we receive the fruit of his labours. Pray today for our Major Archbishop and bishops, his successors.
outline: 1930: communion with Peter, keeping our tradition.
He did not bury what he received.
Love for the Church, prayer, unity.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Visit or pray
If possible, visit the tomb at Pattom; otherwise pray for the Church he founded.
Pray for unity
Pray daily this week for the unity of all the Churches of Kerala.
Trade your talents
Use one gift you have received for the Church instead of burying it.
fathers: St Ignatius of Antioch
Where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the Catholic Church (Letter to the Smyrnaeans 8).
St Cyprian of Carthage
The Church is one, though she spreads far and wide; like the rays of the sun, many, yet one light (On the Unity of the Catholic Church 5).
magis: Orientalium Ecclesiarum 2–3
The Eastern Catholic Churches, holding the same faith, should keep their own rites and traditions whole and entire.
Ut Unum Sint 1
Christ calls all his disciples to unity; the commitment to ecumenism is a duty of the Church.
Catechism 1561
The ordained minister acts in the name of Christ the Head for the building up of the Church.
saints: 16 July: Our Lady of Mount Carmel. Sunday 18 July: IX Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-07-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, the same yesterday, today and forever, we thank you for Archbishop Mar Ivanios, who loved your Church and sought her unity at great cost. Keep our Malankara Church faithful to the faith he lived, bless our Major Archbishop and bishops, make all Christians one, and, if it be your will, glorify your servant. Amen.

2027-07-18.title: Ninth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: Wheat and weeds; mustard seed; yeast
Keep the statutes, for this is your wisdom
Do not associate with the proud
The earth lies polluted; they have broken the covenant
Paul arrives in Rome and takes courage
Those who humble themselves will be exalted
2027-07-18.alt: Season of Pentecost. Remind the faithful that the Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) begins on 1 August in preparation for the Assumption of Mary, Mother of God (15 August).
2027-07-18.verse: For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
theo: At a dinner Jesus watches the guests choosing the places of honour and says: “When you are invited, go and sit down at the lowest place, so that when your host comes, he may say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher’; then you will be honoured in the presence of all who sit at the table with you. For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.” Humility is not thinking little of ourselves; it is letting God decide our place.

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells three small parables of the kingdom. A man sows good seed, but while everyone sleeps an enemy sows weeds among the wheat. The servants want to pull them up at once. The master says: “No; for in gathering the weeds you would uproot the wheat along with them. Let both of them grow together until the harvest.” God is patient. The Church on earth is a field of wheat and weeds; judgment belongs to God at the harvest, not to us now.

The kingdom is also like a mustard seed, “the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches”; and like yeast that a woman mixed into three measures of flour until all of it was leavened. God works through small and hidden things: a family Rosary, a catechism class, one honest worker in an office.

Paul reaches Rome as a prisoner, but believers walk out to meet him, and “on seeing them, Paul thanked God and took courage.” He reminds the Corinthians, who were taking one another to court, of what they had become: “you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.” A humble and patient Church, aware of the grace she has received, will grow like the mustard seed.
conn: Wisdom in obedience.
Deuteronomy 4:6: keeping God's law will make the nations say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and discerning people.”
The proud.
Sirach 13 and Luke 14: pride seeks the high place; God lifts the lowly.
Trust.
Psalm 22:4: “In you our ancestors trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them”; the master's patience in the parable.
The broken covenant.
Isaiah 24:5: the earth defiled by sin; the weeds sown by the enemy.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Lord invites us to his table not because we are worthy but because he is merciful. We come as those who take the lowest place, and he says, “Friend, move up higher.”
outline: Who sits at the top table?
“Those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
live: Take the lower place
Let someone else go first this week: in a queue, a conversation, a decision.
Be patient with the weeds
Stop condemning one person you find difficult; leave judgment to God.
Prepare for Shunoyo
Plan how you will keep the Fifteen Days' Fast from 1 August.
fathers: St Augustine
Do not be in a hurry to separate; many who are weeds today become wheat tomorrow (Sermon 73A).
St John Chrysostom
The Lord forbids the uprooting of the weeds so that no one may be killed; he does not forbid restraining heretics, but forbids killing them (Homilies on Matthew 46).
magis: Catechism 2559
Humility is the foundation of prayer.
Catechism 827
The Church, embracing sinners in her bosom, is at once holy and always in need of purification.
Catechism 1269
The baptised are washed, sanctified and justified; they belong to Christ.
saints: 22 July: St Mary Magdalene. Sunday 25 July: X Sunday after Pentecost. 1 August: the Fifteen Days' Fast begins.
2027-07-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, you lifted up the humble and were patient with the field of wheat and weeds. Teach us to take the lowest place, to leave judgment to you, and to trust the small seeds of your kingdom. Wash, sanctify and justify us in your Spirit, and prepare us to keep the fast in honour of your Mother. Amen.

2027-07-25.title: Tenth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: They all ate and were filled
I am the Lord who heals you
The Lord restored the fortunes of Job
Happy are those who fear the Lord
Paul teaches about the kingdom of God
If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord
2027-07-25.alt: Season of Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary the Tenth Sunday after Pentecost was the Syro-Malankara Catholic Sunday School Day, with the collection and the “cover collection” sent to the eparchial curia for the faith formation of children. The Fifteen Days' Fast begins on Sunday 1 August.
2027-07-25.verse: Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
theo: The disciples ask: “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Jesus calls a child, puts the child among them and says: “Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever becomes humble like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.” Children are not only the future of the Church; they show us now how to trust, to receive, to depend on the Father.

Jesus speaks with great seriousness about harm done to children: “If any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for you if a great millstone were fastened around your neck and you were drowned in the depth of the sea… Take care that you do not despise one of these little ones; for, I tell you, in heaven their angels continually see the face of my Father.” “It is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.” Protecting and forming children is a holy duty of every family and parish.

St Paul gives the heart of what we teach them: “if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. For one believes with the heart and so is justified, and one confesses with the mouth and so is saved… Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Faith is believed in the heart and spoken with the lips. Sunday School exists so that children may learn both.

At Marah the water was bitter, and the people could not drink. God showed Moses a piece of wood; when it was thrown into the water, the water became sweet. Then God said: “I am the LORD who heals you.” The Fathers saw in that wood the Cross, which makes the bitter waters of life sweet. In Rome Paul, a prisoner, “welcomed all who came to him, proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness.” Teachers of the faith carry on his work.
conn: Bitter water made sweet.
Exodus 15:25: the wood thrown into the water; the Cross makes life's bitterness sweet.
Job restored.
Job 42:10: the Lord restored Job when he prayed for his friends.
The just man.
Psalm 112:7: “They are not afraid of evil tidings; their hearts are firm, secure in the LORD.”
Teaching to the end.
Acts 28:30–31: Paul teaches openly in Rome; catechists continue his mission.
altar: Children prepare for First Holy Communion by learning that the Bread of the altar is Jesus himself. Every Qurbono is a lesson in childlike faith: we receive what we could never earn.
outline: Trust, receive, depend on the Father.
Point 2 · Do not despise the little ones
Marah and the Cross; teachers of the faith.
“Unless you change and become like children…”
live: Thank a catechist
Thank your children's Sunday School teacher this week.
Pray with a child
Pray with a child in your family each evening this week.
Prepare for the fast
Decide how your family will keep the Fifteen Days' Fast.
fathers: St Hilary of Poitiers

Children follow their father, love their mother, do not know how to wish evil on their neighbour, do not care for wealth, are not proud: to be like them is to enter the kingdom (Commentary on Matthew 18, 1).
St Ambrose
The wood thrown into the bitter water is the Cross of Christ, which makes the bitter waters sweet (On the Mysteries 3, 14).
magis: Catechism 526
To become a child in relation to God is the condition for entering the kingdom.
Catechism 2226
Education in the faith by the parents should begin in the child's earliest years.
Catechism 185–186
Whoever says “I believe” says “I pledge myself to what we believe”; the profession of faith with the lips.
saints: 28 July: St Alphonsa. 29 July: Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus. 31 July: St Ignatius of Loyola. 1 August: the Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) begins.
2027-07-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, you placed a child in the midst of your disciples. Make us humble and trusting like children; help us protect and form the little ones you love; bless our catechists and Sunday School teachers; and make the bitter waters of our lives sweet by your Cross. Amen.

quick: Thomas moved from doubt to the greatest confession: “My Lord and my God!”
“Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”
Thomas, according to our tradition, brought the Gospel to India: he is our father in faith.
2027-07-03.action: Say “My Lord and my God” at the elevation during Holy Qurbono.
2027-07-03.question: Do I bring my doubts to Jesus, or walk away with them?
2027-07-03.special: Dukrono of St Thomas the Apostle (Saturday): Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: Seven and a half churches are linked by tradition with St Thomas in Kerala: Kodungallur, Palayur, Kottakkavu, Kokkamangalam, Niranam, Nilackal, Kollam and Thiruvithamcode. For almost two thousand years families have handed on the faith from parents to children. We are the fruit of one apostle's courage.

family.explain: Thomas said he would only believe if he could touch Jesus' wounds. When Jesus came, Thomas said: “My Lord and my God!” Later he came to India and told our ancestors about Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for St Thomas and pray for the Church in India.
family.ask: Ask: “What questions do we have about God? Let's ask Jesus together.”

kidsaint: Thomas was brave: when Jesus went toward danger he said, “Let us also go, that we may die with him” (John 11:16). He had doubts, but when he met the risen Jesus he believed with all his heart, and according to tradition he travelled all the way to India. Lesson: honest questions can lead to strong faith.
term: Syriac for “remembrance, commemoration”: the feast of a saint, especially the anniversary of death or the translation of relics. The Dukrono of St Thomas is kept on 3 July.
termMore: The ancient name of the St Thomas Christians of Kerala, who trace their faith to the preaching of St Thomas. The Syro-Malankara and Syro-Malabar Churches are both heirs of this tradition.

quick: “A house divided against itself cannot stand”: Satan divides, Christ unites.
The sin against the Spirit is refusing God's mercy; guard your words.
“He is our peace”: Christ breaks down every dividing wall.
2027-07-04.action: Take one concrete step toward reconciliation in your family or parish this week.
2027-07-04.question: Where am I contributing to division, and where can I build peace?
illus: In many Kerala villages two branches of one ancient Thomas Christian family worship in different churches across the same road. When they pray together at a funeral or a wedding, people say: this is how it should always be. Christ came to break down dividing walls.

family.explain: Jesus says a house where people fight against each other cannot stand. Families are strong when they forgive and stay together.
family.intention: We pray for peace and unity in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to make peace with?”

kidsaint: An Italian girl of eleven who was attacked and mortally wounded by a young man named Alessandro. Before she died she forgave him. Years later he repented, and was present when she was declared a saint. Lesson: forgiveness can change even a hard heart.
term: The “unforgivable” sin of Mark 3:29: not a sin too big for God's mercy, but the deliberate, final refusal of that mercy, which closes the heart to forgiveness (CCC 1864).
termMore: In the Syro-Malankara Qurbono the peace (Shlomo) is passed from the altar through the congregation before the anaphora, as a sign of reconciliation before offering the sacrifice (Matthew 5:23–24).

quick: “The word of God is living and active”: Christ speaks when the Gospel is proclaimed.
Good soil hears the word, accepts it, and bears fruit a hundredfold.
Jesus is a high priest who understands our weakness: approach with boldness.
2027-07-11.action: Read the Sunday Gospel again for ten minutes each day this week.
2027-07-11.question: Do I really listen when God's word is read?
2027-07-11.special: Eighth Sunday after Pentecost. Thursday 15 July: Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios, Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: In many Kerala homes the Bible is placed on a stand with a lamp beside it, honoured like a guest. Honouring the Book is good; opening it every day is better. The word works only in the heart that listens.

family.explain: God's word is alive! When we read the Bible, God speaks to our hearts like a friend.
family.intention: We pray to listen to God's word every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What did God say to us in today's Gospel?”

catechism: Scripture in the life of the Church.
The common priesthood of the faithful.
kidsaint: A young man who left the noisy city to pray in a cave, and later founded monasteries where monks prayed and worked. His Rule begins with the word “Listen.” Lesson: to hear God, we need quiet hearts.
term: In the Syro-Malankara Qurbono the Gospel (Evangelion) is proclaimed by the priest with candles and incense, and the people stand, because Christ himself speaks.
termMore: All the baptised share in Christ's priesthood (1 Peter 2:9): they offer their lives, prayers and work as spiritual sacrifices. This common priesthood differs in essence, not only in degree, from the ministerial priesthood of bishops and priests (Lumen Gentium 10).

quick: Mar Ivanios sought the unity of the Church and entered communion with Peter in 1930, keeping our liturgy.
Like the faithful servant, he traded the talents he received.
2027-07-15.action: Pray each day this week for the unity of the Churches in Kerala.
2027-07-15.question: What would I be ready to give up for the truth and unity of the Church?
2027-07-15.special: Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios (Thursday): Holy Qurbono for the people. Pilgrimage to St Mary's Cathedral, Pattom.
illus: After the reunion of 1930 Mar Ivanios and his companions had no cathedral and no properties. They celebrated the Qurbono in sheds and borrowed rooms. Today the Syro-Malankara Catholic Church has eparchies across India and in the diaspora. The seed sown in poverty grew.

family.explain: We remember good leaders who taught us about God, like Mar Ivanios, who gave up a lot so that our Church could be united with the Pope.
family.intention: We pray for our Church and for the unity of all Christians.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught us about God? Let's thank God for them.”

kidsaint: A clever teacher who loved to pray and started a community called Bethany. He wanted all Christians to be one family with the Pope, and in 1930 he joined the Catholic Church even though he lost his churches and money. Lesson: love Jesus and his Church more than comfort.
term: The movement led by Mar Ivanios through which, in 1930, part of the Malankara Church entered full communion with the Catholic Church while keeping its West Syriac (Antiochene) liturgy and traditions.
termMore: The Order of the Imitation of Christ (Bethany Ashram), founded by Mar Ivanios in 1919, and the Sisters of the Imitation of Christ (Bethany Madhom), founded in 1925: religious communities of the Syro-Malankara Church devoted to prayer, education and mission.

quick: “Those who humble themselves will be exalted”: let God choose our place.
Wheat and weeds grow together until the harvest: God is patient.
The kingdom grows from small hidden things, like mustard seed and yeast.
2027-07-18.action: Let someone else go first each day this week.
2027-07-18.question: Where am I seeking the highest place?
2027-07-18.special: Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. Announce the Fifteen Days' Fast (Shunoyo Nombu) from 1 August.
illus: A Kerala farmer who pulls the young weeds from a paddy field too early tears out the rice seedlings with them. He waits until both are grown and the difference is clear. God is the wise farmer of our hearts and of his Church.

family.explain: Jesus says not to rush for the best seat. Be humble, and God will lift you up.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we let others go first this week?”

kidsaint: Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus who stayed near the cross when others ran away. On Easter morning she was the first to see the risen Jesus, and he sent her to tell the apostles. Lesson: Jesus loves humble, faithful hearts.
term: The Fifteen Days' Fast (1–15 August) kept by the Syro-Malankara Church before the feast of the Shunoyo, the Assumption (Dormition) of the Mother of God into heaven.
termMore: Matthew 13 gathers seven parables: the sower, the weeds, the mustard seed, the yeast, the treasure, the pearl and the net. Together they show that the kingdom begins small and hidden, grows by God's power, and is completed at the harvest.

quick: “Unless you change and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom.”
Do not despise the little ones; their angels see the Father's face.
“If you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord… you will be saved.”
2027-07-25.action: Thank your children's Sunday School teacher this week.
2027-07-25.question: In what way do I need to become more like a child before God?
2027-07-25.special: Tenth Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26: Sunday School Day; collection and cover collection for children's faith formation. Check your eparchy's circular.) The Fifteen Days' Fast begins next Sunday, 1 August.
illus: In Kerala parishes thousands of young people give up their Sunday mornings to teach catechism to children for no pay. One former student, now a doctor, said: “I forgot my school teachers' names, but I never forgot the teacher who taught me to pray.”

family.explain: Jesus put a child in the middle of the grown-ups and said: be like this child! Children trust God like a little one trusts mum and dad.
family.intention: We pray for all children and for those who teach them the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “What can grown-ups learn from children about trusting God?”

catechism: Parents as first teachers of the faith.
kidsaint: A sister from Bharananganam in Kerala who was often sick and suffered a lot, but offered everything to Jesus with a smile. She loved children and prayed for everyone. She was the first woman from India to be declared a saint (2008). Lesson: we can offer our pains to Jesus with love.
term: The parish faith-formation programme in which children and teenagers learn the Bible, prayers, the sacraments and the teachings of the Church each Sunday. The Syro-Malankara Catholic Sunday School observes a day of prayer and support every year.
termMore: Jesus says the angels of the little ones “continually see the face of my Father” (Matthew 18:10). The Church teaches that from infancy to death human life is surrounded by the watchful care and intercession of angels (CCC 336).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate our father in faith, St Thomas. We often call him “doubting Thomas,” but the Gospel shows more. When Jesus decided to go to Judea, where they wanted to stone him, it was Thomas who said: “Let us also go, that we may die with him.” He was brave and honest.

On Easter evening he was absent. He would not simply accept the others' word: “Unless I see the mark of the nails… I will not believe.” A week later Jesus came and said: “Put your finger here and see my hands… Do not doubt but believe.” And Thomas fell down: “My Lord and my God!” No one in the Gospels says it more clearly: Jesus is not only teacher or prophet; he is Lord and God.

Jesus said: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That is us. Our ancestors in Kerala did not see Jesus, but they believed the word of Thomas, who had seen and touched. And according to our tradition, Thomas sealed that word with his blood at Mylapore.

So today let us thank God for the faith we received. Let us not be ashamed of it in our schools, offices and on social media. And when doubt comes, do not run away from Jesus; bring it to him, as Thomas did. At this Qurbono, when the Holy Mysteries are raised, say in your heart with Thomas: “My Lord and my God.” Amen.
kids: Children, St Thomas was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. He said he would not believe Jesus was alive unless he could touch his wounds!
Then Jesus came and showed him. Thomas said: “My Lord and my God!”
Later, Thomas travelled all the way to India to tell people about Jesus. That's why we are Christians today! Let's say with Thomas: “My Lord and my God!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, when Jesus drove out demons, his enemies said he was working with Satan. Jesus answered: “If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.” The devil's work is division: between husband and wife, parents and children, neighbours, parishes, even Churches. The Spirit's work is communion.

Then Jesus warns about the sin against the Holy Spirit, which can never be forgiven. People sometimes fear they have committed it. But the Church teaches: God's mercy has no limits. This sin is to refuse that mercy to the end, to call the Spirit's work evil and close the door. If you are worried that you have committed it, that very worry shows you have not. And Jesus adds: “by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.” Our tongues can build or destroy.

St Paul says: Christ “is our peace; he has broken down the dividing wall of hostility.” Through his blood those who were far off have been brought near. We who were strangers are now members of God's household, built on the apostles with Christ as the cornerstone.

When the first Christians were threatened, they did not divide; they prayed together, and the place was shaken, and they were filled with the Holy Spirit. Let us do the same. This week take one step to heal a division: a phone call, an apology, a visit. Guard your words. And pray for the unity of all the children of St Thomas. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: a house where everyone fights cannot stand. It falls down!
Jesus wants our families to be strong, with people who forgive each other and help each other.
Is there someone you quarrelled with? Can you say sorry this week? Let's pray: “Jesus, make our family one!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Letter to the Hebrews says: “The word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword.” When the Gospel is read in the Holy Qurbono, it is not a story from long ago. Christ himself speaks to us now. That is why we stand, why the candles and the incense honour the Book.

In Mark's Gospel Jesus begins his parable with one word: “Listen!” and ends with another: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!” In between is the sower. The same seed falls on the path, on rock, among thorns, and on good soil. Good soil is the heart that hears the word, accepts it, and lets it bear fruit, thirty, sixty, a hundredfold.

At the burning bush God told Moses his name: “I AM WHO I AM.” The living God speaks. Jeremiah says that God asked only one thing of Israel: “Obey my voice.” To obey means to listen deeply. Much of our trouble comes from not listening: to God, to one another.

And if we are afraid that the Word will judge us, Hebrews adds: we have a high priest who understands our weakness, who was tested in every way as we are, yet without sin. “Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy.” This week give ten minutes each day to the Gospel. Listen. And let the word bear fruit. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once began a story with one word: “Listen!” Can you say it? Listen!
A farmer threw seeds. Some fell on the path, some on rocks, some in thorns, and some in good soil. The good soil gave lots and lots of fruit!
God's word is the seed, and your heart is the soil. Let's listen to Jesus every day and be good soil!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Letter to the Hebrews tells us: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” Today our Church remembers her father, Archbishop Mar Ivanios, who went to God on 15 July 1953.

He was a scholar and teacher, but above all a man of prayer. He founded Bethany, the communities of the Imitation of Christ. And he carried a great longing: that the ancient Malankara Church be one with the Church of Peter. On 20 September 1930, with Mar Theophilos and a few others, he entered full communion with the Catholic Church, keeping the beautiful liturgy of our fathers.

It cost him a great deal. He left behind churches, properties and friendships. He began again in small chapels and sheds. But he trusted the promise God made to Moses: “I will be with you.” Like the faithful servant in the parable, he did not bury his talents. Today our Church, spread across India and the world, is the harvest of that sacrifice.

So let us imitate his faith: love for prayer, love for the liturgy, love for the unity of the Church. Let us pray for our Major Archbishop and bishops, for all Christians of Kerala to be one, and, if it is God's will, for the glorification of his servant Mar Ivanios. “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” Amen.
kids: Children, today we remember Mar Ivanios, the father of our Malankara Catholic Church.
He loved Jesus and wanted all Christians to be one family with the Pope. He gave up big churches and a lot of money to do this!
Let's thank God for him and pray: “Jesus, make all Christians one family!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Jesus is at a dinner and notices the guests rushing for the best seats. He says: Sit in the lowest place, and let the host call you higher. “For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.” In families, parishes and offices there is often a quiet competition for the best seat. Jesus offers us freedom: let God decide your place.

In the evening Gospel a farmer's enemy sows weeds among his wheat. The servants want to pull them out at once. The master says: no, you will pull out the wheat too; let them grow together until the harvest. We are often impatient servants. We want to separate the good and the bad in the Church and in our families right now. But God is patient. Many who look like weeds today will become wheat tomorrow. Judgment belongs to him.

Then Jesus speaks of the tiny mustard seed that becomes a tree, and of the yeast hidden in flour. God's kingdom grows quietly: a mother's prayer, a catechism class on Sunday morning, a young person's honest word. Do not despise small beginnings.

St Paul reminds the Corinthians: “you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.” Remember who you are. And remember: on 1 August the Fifteen Days' Fast begins, in honour of our Mother's Assumption. Let us prepare our hearts with humility. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: when you go to a party, don't run for the best chair! Sit in a simple place, and the host may say, “Come up here, friend!”
He also told a story about a tiny mustard seed that grew into a big tree where birds could build nests.
Small kind acts can grow big too! This week, let someone else go first.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the disciples asked Jesus: “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?” Jesus did not answer with a name. He called a child and stood the child among them: “Unless you change and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.” A child trusts, receives, asks, and is not ashamed of needing help. That is how we must stand before God.

Then Jesus speaks very strongly: whoever causes one of these little ones to stumble would be better off with a millstone around his neck in the depths of the sea. Their angels always see the Father's face. Children are precious to God. Every family and every parish must protect them, form them, and never give them scandal by our lives.

St Paul tells us what we must teach them: “if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.” That is the work of our Sunday School teachers, who give their Sunday mornings to teach our children the faith. Let us thank them and pray for them today.

At Marah the water was bitter; God showed Moses a piece of wood, and the water became sweet. The Fathers saw there the Cross, which makes the bitterness of life sweet. Let us teach our children to love the Cross and the Lord who heals. And next Sunday, 1 August, we begin the Fifteen Days' Fast in honour of our Mother's Assumption. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus says something wonderful about you! The disciples asked who is the greatest, and Jesus put a child in the middle and said: “Be like this child!”
You trust God like you trust your mum and dad. That makes Jesus very happy.
Today, say thank you to your Sunday School teacher! And let's pray: “Jesus, I believe you are Lord!”

intro: We keep the Dukrono of St Thomas, our Father in Faith. The apostle who first doubted made the fullest confession of faith in the Gospels and carried it to India. We are the fruit of his mission.

points.h: From doubt to the fullest confession
sub: Job longed to find God; Thomas wanted to touch the wounds.
Jesus comes back for one disciple and offers his wounds.
Thomas confesses: “My Lord and my God!” The risen Jesus is truly God.
q: Oh, that I knew where I might find him, that I might come even to his dwelling!
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!” Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”
points.apply: At the elevation in the Holy Qurbono, say silently: “My Lord and my God.”

points.h: The Way, the Truth and the Life
sub: Thomas asked: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
His honest question drew from Jesus one of the greatest sayings of the Gospel.
The path of those who follow Christ grows brighter like the dawn.
q: But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Bring your honest questions about faith to the Lord in prayer, and to a priest or catechist.

sub: Isaiah praised the feet of the messenger of peace.
As the Father sent the Son, Christ sends his apostles; tradition holds that Thomas came to India and was martyred at Mylapore.
The St Thomas Christians received his faith; we are called to hand it on.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.”
points.apply: Teach a child in your family the confession “My Lord and my God.”

concl: Thomas shows that honest doubt can become deep faith when it meets the wounds of Christ.
Let us confess him as Lord and God and carry the faith of our fathers forward.
2027-07-03.resolve: Pray for the Church in India and for missionaries from Kerala serving abroad.

intro: Jesus warns that a house divided against itself cannot stand. Paul proclaims that Christ has broken down the dividing wall. The Spirit who shook the place where the apostles prayed gives us boldness and unity.

sub: Satan divides; Christ gathers.
Division in hearts, families and parishes weakens our witness.
God promises peace to those far off and those near, and healing.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand. And if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
points.apply: Take the first step to heal one division in your family or neighbourhood.

points.h: Christ breaks down the dividing wall
sub: The Day of Atonement prefigured the cleansing Christ would bring.
By his cross Christ has made Jew and Gentile one, broken down the wall of hostility.
We pray and work for the unity of all Christians, as our Church has done from the reunion of 1930.
q: For on this day atonement shall be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins you shall be clean before the LORD.
For he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us.
points.apply: Pray this week for Christian unity, especially among the Churches of Kerala.

points.h: Our words and the Holy Spirit
sub: Jesus warns against blasphemy against the Holy Spirit: not a sin too great for mercy, but the refusal of mercy itself (CCC 1864).
Every careless word will be accounted for; words can give life or destroy.
Filled with the Spirit, the apostles spoke God's word with boldness.
q: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruits.
I tell you, on the day of judgment you will have to give an account for every careless word you utter; for by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
points.apply: Fast from gossip and harsh words for one week.

concl: Christ unites what sin divides; the Spirit gives words that build up.
Let us be peacemakers in our homes and bold witnesses in the world.
2027-07-04.resolve: Pray Psalm 133 as a family each evening this week.

intro: Theme: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen.”
Jesus tells the parable of the sower. The Letter to the Hebrews calls God's word living and active. The God who revealed his name to Moses speaks to us, and calls us his own priestly people.

sub: God's word never returns empty; the problem is never the seed.
The path, the rocky ground and the thorns are hearts closed by hardness, shallowness or worry.
Good soil hears, accepts and bears fruit with patience.
q: So shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.
points.apply: Ask yourself honestly which soil your heart is this week, and remove one “thorn”.

points.h: The word is living and active
sub: God asks above all: “Obey my voice.”
His word judges the thoughts of the heart; it is a sword that heals.
In the Holy Qurbono, when the Gospel is proclaimed, Christ himself speaks (Second Vatican Council, Sacrosanctum Concilium 7).
q: But this command I gave them, “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk only in the way that I command you, so that it may be well with you.”

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again at home and keep one verse in your heart.

points.h: A people who belong to “I AM”
sub: God revealed his name to Moses: “I AM WHO I AM.”
Through baptism we become a chosen race, a royal priesthood.
This common priesthood of the faithful is lived by offering our lives with Christ, and is served by the ministerial priesthood.
q: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” He said further, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Offer your daily work to God each morning as your spiritual sacrifice.

concl: The Sower is generous; the word is powerful; the harvest depends on our listening.
Let us be good soil and a priestly people.
2027-07-11.resolve: Give ten minutes each day this week to reading the Gospel of Mark.

intro: Theme: “Remember your leaders; imitate their faith.”

Today we remember Archbishop Geevarghese Mar Ivanios (died 15 July 1953), founder of the Bethany Ashram and Bethany Sisters, who led the reunion of 1930 and became the first Metropolitan Archbishop of our Church. His cause for canonisation is in progress; we honour him as Servant of God.

sub: God promised Moses: “I will be with you.” He keeps that promise to those he calls to lead.
Mar Ivanios sought the truth of the Church in prayer and study, and followed it at great cost.
We remember him not with nostalgia but by imitating his faith in Christ, who is the same forever.
q: He said, “I will be with you; and this shall be the sign for you that it is I who sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall worship God on this mountain.”
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
points.apply: Read a short account of the reunion of 1930 with your family.

sub: The master entrusts talents to servants and asks for fruit.
Mar Ivanios used his gifts for prayer, education and the unity of the Church.
Every gift we have is entrusted to us for the Lord's work.
q: With all your soul fear the Lord, and revere his priests.
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and trustworthy slave; you have been trustworthy in a few things, I will put you in charge of many things; enter into the joy of your master.’
points.apply: Name one talent God has given you and use it this week for the Church.

sub: God promised shepherds after his own heart.
Paul urged the elders to keep watch over the flock bought by Christ's blood.
We pray for our bishops and priests, and for vocations to the Bethany communities and our seminaries.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son.
points.apply: Pray today for the cause of Mar Ivanios, leaving the judgement to the Church.

concl: Mar Ivanios teaches that faithfulness to truth and love of unity can shape a whole Church.
Let us remember, imitate and pray.
2027-07-15.resolve: If possible, visit or pray for the tomb at St Mary's Cathedral, Pattom.

intro: Theme: “The lowest place and the hidden seed.”

At a dinner Jesus teaches humility; in the parables he shows how God's kingdom grows quietly, patiently, from small beginnings. In two weeks the Fifteen Days' Fast in honour of the Mother of God begins.

sub: Guests rush for places of honour; Jesus tells them to sit at the lowest.
Humility is not thinking little of ourselves but seeing ourselves truly before God.
The greater one's position, the greater the need for humility.
q: The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; so you will find favor in the sight of the Lord.
For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: This week let someone else have the honour, the credit or the last word.

points.h: Wheat and weeds: the patience of God
sub: Good and evil grow together in the world and even in the Church until the harvest.
God is patient, giving time for repentance; judgement belongs to him.
Our task is not to uproot others but to be wheat.
q: Through such works you have taught your people that the righteous must be kind, and you have filled your children with good hope, because you give repentance for sins.
Let both of them grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Collect the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.
points.apply: Replace one judgemental thought about someone with a prayer for them.

sub: The kingdom begins small and grows great; it works quietly like yeast.
Keeping God's law faithfully is Israel's wisdom before the nations; our faithful lives are a witness too.
Mary, the humble handmaid, is the perfect example of this hidden growth.
q: You must observe them diligently, for this will show your wisdom and discernment to the peoples, who, when they hear all these statutes, will say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and discerning people!”

The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field; it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.
points.apply: Begin now to plan how your family will keep the Fifteen Days' Fast from 1 August.

concl: God's kingdom grows through the humble, the patient and the faithful in small things.
Let us take the lowest place, trust God's patience, and be yeast in the world.
2027-07-18.resolve: Pray the Magnificat (Luke 1:46–55) each evening this week.

intro: Jesus places a child in the midst of his disciples and teaches that the humble are the greatest. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was Sunday School Day: a day to thank catechists and renew our duty to hand on the faith.

sub: The disciples ask who is the greatest; Jesus answers with a child.
Childlike faith trusts, depends on the Father, and receives everything as gift.
Like a child quiet at its mother's side, the soul rests in God.
q: But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child that is with me.
Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever becomes humble like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent, trusting prayer each night before sleep.

points.h: Do not lose one of these little ones
sub: Moses commanded parents to teach God's words at home, on the road, at rest and at rising.
The Father does not want even one little one to be lost.
Parents are the first catechists; Sunday school helps but cannot replace the home (CCC 2223–2226).
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
points.apply: Thank your children's catechists, and pray with your children every evening.

points.h: Confess with your lips, be healed
sub: God revealed himself as the Lord who heals.
Faith must be confessed openly: Jesus is Lord.
Children learn to confess Christ by seeing adults do it without shame.
q: I will not bring upon you any of the diseases that I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the LORD who heals you.
Because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross before meals, even in public.

concl: The kingdom belongs to the childlike, and children belong to the kingdom.
Let us become little before God and great in our care for the little ones.
2027-07-25.resolve: Support Sunday school generously, and begin family preparation for the Fifteen Days' Fast next Sunday.
